{{short description|Geometric object}}
[[File:Couronne solide.svg|thumb|The '''spherinder''' can be seen as the volume between two parallel and equal solid 2-[[sphere]]s (3-balls) in 4-dimensional space, here stereographically projected into 3D.]]
In [[Four-dimensional space|four-dimensional geometry]], the '''spherinder''', or '''spherical cylinder''' or '''spherical prism''', is a geometric object, defined as the [[Cartesian product]] of a 3-[[ball (mathematics)|ball]] (or solid 2-[[sphere]]) of radius ''r''<sub>1</sub> and a [[line segment]] of length 2''r''<sub>2</sub>:

:<math>D = \{ (x,y,z,w) | x^2+y^2+z^2\leq r_1^2,\ w^2\leq r_2^2 \}</math>

Like the [[duocylinder]], it is also analogous to a [[Cylinder (geometry)|cylinder]] in 3-space, which is the Cartesian product of a disk with a [[line segment]]. It is a [[rotatope]] and a [[toratope]].

It can be seen in 3-dimensional space by [[stereographic projection]] as two concentric spheres, in a similar way that a [[tesseract]] (cubic prism) can be projected as two concentric cubes, and how a [[circular cylinder]] can be projected into 2-dimensional space as two concentric circles.

== Spherindrical coordinate system ==
One can define a "spherindrical" coordinate system {{Math|(''r'', ''θ'', ''φ'', ''w'')}}, consisting of [[spherical coordinates]] with an extra coordinate {{Mvar|w}}. This is analogous to how [[cylindrical coordinates]] are defined: {{Mvar|r}} and {{Mvar|φ}} being [[Polar coordinate system|polar coordinates]] with an elevation coordinate {{Mvar|z}}. Spherindrical coordinates can be converted to Cartesian coordinates using the formulas <math display="block">\begin{align} 
x &= r \cos \varphi \sin \theta \\ 
y &= r \sin \varphi \sin \theta \\ 
z &= r \cos \theta \\
w &= w
\end{align}</math> where {{Mvar|r}} is the radius, {{Mvar|θ}} is the zenith angle, {{Mvar|φ}} is the azimuthal angle, and {{Mvar|w}} is the height. Cartesian coordinates can be converted to spherindrical coordinates using the formulas <math display="block">\begin{align} 
r &= \sqrt{x^2+y^2+z^2} \\ 
\varphi &= \arctan{\frac{y}{x}} \\ 
\theta &= \arccot{\frac{z}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}}} \\
w &= w
\end{align}</math>The [[Volume element|hypervolume element]] for spherindrical coordinates is <math>\mathrm{d}H = r^2\sin{\theta}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\,\mathrm{d}\varphi\,\mathrm{d}w,</math> which can be derived by computing the [[Jacobian matrix and determinant|Jacobian]].

== Measurements ==

=== Hypervolume ===
Given a spherinder with a spherical base of radius {{Mvar|r}} and a height {{Mvar|h}}, the hypervolume of the spherinder is given by <math display="block">H=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 h</math>

=== Surface volume ===
The surface volume of a spherinder, like the surface area of a cylinder, is made up of three parts:

* the volume of the top base: <math display="inline">\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3</math>
* the volume of the bottom base: <math display="inline">\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3</math>
* the volume of the lateral 3D surface: <math display="inline">4 \pi r^2 h</math>, which is the surface area of the spherical base times the height


Therefore, the total surface volume is 

<math display="block">SV=\frac{8}{3}\pi r^3 + 4\pi r^2 h</math>

=== Proof ===

The above formulas for hypervolume and surface volume can be proven using integration. The hypervolume of an arbitrary 4D region is given by the quadruple integral <math display="block">H=\iiiint\limits_{D} \mathrm{d}H</math>

The hypervolume of the spherinder can be integrated over spherindrical coordinates. <math display="block">H_\mathrm{spherinder}=\iiiint\limits_{D} \mathrm{d}H = \int_{0}^{h}\int_{0}^{2\pi}\int_{0}^{\pi}\int_{0}^{R}r^2\sin{\theta}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\,\mathrm{d}\varphi\,\mathrm{d}w = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 h</math>

== Related 4-polytopes ==
[[File:Truncated icosidodecahedral prism.png|thumb|The related [[truncated icosidodecahedral prism]] is constructed from two [[truncated icosidodecahedron|truncated icosidodecahedra]] connected by [[prism (geometry)|prisms]], shown here in [[stereographic projection]] with some prisms hidden.]]
The spherinder is related to the [[Uniform polychoron#Prismatic uniform polychora|uniform prismatic polychora]], which are [[Cartesian product]]s of a regular or semiregular [[polyhedron]] and a [[line segment]]. There are eighteen convex uniform prisms based on the [[Platonic solid|Platonic]] and [[Archimedean solid]]s ([[tetrahedral prism]], [[truncated tetrahedral prism]], [[cubic prism]], [[cuboctahedral prism]], [[octahedral prism]], [[rhombicuboctahedral prism]], [[truncated cubic prism]], [[truncated octahedral prism]], [[truncated cuboctahedral prism]], [[snub cubic prism]], [[dodecahedral prism]], [[icosidodecahedral prism]], [[icosahedral prism]], [[truncated dodecahedral prism]], [[rhombicosidodecahedral prism]], [[truncated icosahedral prism]], [[truncated icosidodecahedral prism]], [[snub dodecahedral prism]]), plus an infinite family based on [[antiprism]]s, and another infinite family of uniform [[duoprism]]s, which are products of two [[regular polygon]]s.
